subject: Fee harmonizer / escape matrix — revised redline and ask
messages:
From: Jay Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on "Fee Harmonizer" language (Exhibit B)

Markus —

Thanks for the draft order form. Our procurement team has one substantive ask on Exhibit B (the fee harmonizer / annual adjustment language). The short version: we need a clear cap on year-over-year percentage increases and an explicit escape matrix that triggers if our usage falls >30% in a rolling 12-month window. That protects our budget planning and gives us a path to unwind if adoption stalls.

I've attached Acme's proposed redline to make the point (acme_initial_redline.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a 12% annual cap and include a 30% drop escape that maps to prorated minimums rather than an immediate termination? If not, please propose alternative guardrails.

Also, a practical note — our SOW team wants to see the order schedule workbook with mapped SKUs so they can reconcile with internal billing.

Appreciate a quick read — we are targeting internal signoff by Nov 10.

Jay Sullivan
Director, Procurement
Acme Systems

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jay Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on "Fee Harmonizer" language (Exhibit B)

Jay —

Thanks for the redline and the clarity on timing. We're aligned on the intent (budget protection + sensible unwind path). A few quick points:

- Cap: We can accept a fixed annual increase cap capped at 12% provided the metric is clearly defined (we propose: list price increase applied to the prior contract year billing, not to projected usage).
- Escape matrix: We don't do immediate termination for an adoption dip under 30% — our preference is a staged remediation: a 90-day remediation window, then a temporary minimum-commit reduction (prorated) for the next 12 months, with a single true-up at the end of that period.
- Practical mapping: rather than a binary 30% trigger, we prefer a graded matrix (30–50%: 25% minimum reduction; >50%: 50% minimum reduction + review). That preserves predictability for both sides.

I've attached our proposed markup: rwi_exhibit_b_fee_harmonizer_markus_redline.docx. It implements the 12% cap and the graded escape matrix, and it includes the remediation steps and true-up mechanics. The order_schedule_v3.xlsx contains the SKU-to-metric map the SOW team requested.

Marissa/ Karthik — can you both weigh-in on whether legal is OK with the staged remediation wording and the prorated true-up timing (12 months)? If legal prefers an immediate termination carveout, flag that and propose the shortest remediation period you can accept.

Jay — if that approach sounds reasonable, I'll send the revised exhibit with a DocuSign envelope for the order form and the updated order schedule.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on "Fee Harmonizer" language (Exhibit B)

Markus / Karthik —

Quick internal notes (forwarding Jay's original so thread continuity is kept):

On Mon, Nov 1, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jay Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.com> wrote:
> Markus —
> 
> Thanks for the draft order form....

- Legal: staged remediation + 12-month prorated true-up is clean and operationally implementable. One ask: the remediation notice should include usage telemetry windows (we need to define the lookback: rolling 12 months ending on the notice date).
- Billing: the SKU mapping in order_schedule_v3.xlsx must include the metric column (tokens/units vs seats). Please ensure per-SKU billing unit is explicit to avoid annualized vs monthly misalignment.
- Commercial: the graded matrix is negotiable; I recommend keep thresholds at 30% and 50% but cap the maximum prorated reduction at 50% of committed minimums. No immediate termination language unless fraud or material breach.

Karthik — can you provide the exact telemetry definition we should reference (e.g., "billable tokens consumed as recorded in our usage logs, aggregated per calendar day, 365-day rolling sum"). We should be precise to avoid downstream disputes.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jay Sullivan <j.sullivan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Revised Exhibit B + Order Schedule (DocuSign) — next steps

Jay —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per Marissa and Karthik's input, we've updated Exhibit B to: 1) accept a hard 12% annual increase cap (applies to list price on prior contract year billings), 2) implement the graded escape matrix (30% and 50% thresholds) with staged remediation (90 days) and a 12-month prorated minimum-commit reduction (max 50% reduction), and 3) define the telemetry lookback as "billable tokens consumed as recorded in Redwood usage logs, aggregated per calendar day, 365-day rolling sum ending on the notice date."

I've attached: rwi_exhibit_b_fee_harmonizer_markus_redline.docx and order_schedule_v3.xlsx. The DocuSign envelope is live here: https://www.docusign.com/links/RCQ-ACME-2026-105 — please review the exhibit and the SKU map. If the exhibit looks good to Acme, authorize the envelope and we will route for signature.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm acceptance or provide a single list of items (max 3) we should address before DocuSign.
- We: if accepted, finalize envelope and attach order schedule; if additional items, we will aim to incorporate and re-send within 48 business hours.

Goal: get the order form countersigned and schedule ingested by Nov 12 so procurement can close their internal cycle.

Thanks — talk soon.

Markus Klein
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
